mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly defines average power?

options.A: Average power is the total work done divided by the total time taken.
options.B: Average power is the force applied multiplied by the distance covered.
options.C: Average power is the change in kinetic energy per unit displacement.
options.D: Average power is the work done per unit mass.

mcqs.answer: Average power is the total work done divided by the total time taken.
mcqs.explanation: Average power (P_avg) is defined as the total work done (W) divided by the total time interval (t) during which the work is done, i.e., P_avg = W / t. Option A states this definition correctly. Options B, C, and D describe other quantities (force·distance, energy per displacement, work per mass) and are not definitions of average power.

mcqs.question: A particle experiences a time‑dependent force F = 3t^2 N along its direction of motion. Its velocity at time t is v = 2t m s⁻¹. What is the instantaneous power of the force at t = 2 s?
mcqs.explanation: Instantaneous power P = F·v. At t = 2 s, F = 3(2)^2 = 12 N and v = 2(2) = 4 m/s. Thus P = 12 N × 4 m/s = 48 W. Option B matches this value; the other options result from incorrect multiplication or omission of the time dependence.

mcqs.question: A machine does 500 J of work in 25 s. What is its power?
mcqs.explanation: Power P = work done (W) divided by time (t). Here P = 500 J / 25 s = 20 J/s = 20 W. Option B is correct; the other options arise from mis‑division.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate power to force and velocity
mcqs.question: Which expression correctly relates instantaneous power P to the instantaneous force F acting on a particle and its instantaneous velocity v?
mcqs.explanation: Instantaneous power is the scalar product of force and velocity: P = F·v. This gives the rate at which the force does work. Option C states this relationship. Options A, B, and D are algebraic combinations that have no physical meaning for power.

mcqs.question: Select the correct definition of average power.

options.A: Average power is the work done per unit distance.
options.B: Average power is the total work done divided by the total time taken.
options.C: Average power is the force applied multiplied by the time interval.
options.D: Average power is the energy transferred per unit mass.

mcqs.answer: Average power is the total work done divided by the total time taken.
mcqs.explanation: Average power measures how quickly energy is transferred, defined as P_avg = total work / total time. Option B captures this definition precisely. Options A, C, and D describe unrelated quantities (work per distance, impulse, and specific energy).

mcqs.question: A car engine exerts a constant force of 4000 N and moves the car at a constant speed of 20 m s⁻¹. What is the instantaneous power delivered by the engine?
mcqs.explanation: Instantaneous power P = F·v. Substituting the given values: P = 4000 N × 20 m/s = 80,000 W = 8×10⁴ W. Option B is correct; the other options correspond to incorrect multiplication or missing a zero.

mcqs.question: A crane lifts a 2000 kg load vertically through a height of 10 m in 5 s. Assuming g = 9.8 m s⁻², what is the average power output of the crane during this lift?
mcqs.explanation: Work done against gravity: W = mgh = 2000 kg × 9.8 m/s² × 10 m = 196,000 J. Average power P_avg = W / t = 196,000 J / 5 s = 39,200 W = 39.2 kW. Option B matches this calculation. The other options arise from halving or doubling the correct value.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate power to force and velocity
mcqs.question: A conveyor belt moves at a constant speed of 3 m s⁻¹ while a load on it experiences a constant opposing frictional force of 150 N. What is the minimum mechanical power that must be supplied to the belt to overcome this friction?
mcqs.explanation: Power required to counteract friction: P = F·v = 150 N × 3 m/s = 450 W. Option D is correct. Options A, B, and C correspond to using only part of the product (e.g., dividing by speed or using half the force).
